text:
Marta (Support): multiple customers reporting 502/504 and request timeouts for the hosted generation API starting ~20:05 UTC. flags from eu-central-1 and us-west-2. reproduce locally with curl. adding @Roxanne and @Arjun to triage.

Marta (Support): gateway sample log: 
```
2026-03-15T20:06:08Z ERROR gateway req=req_zeta route=/v1/generate status=502 upstream=memcached://cache-prefix-read:11211 err="read tcp 10.8.2.4:53922->10.9.3.11:11211: i/o timeout"
```

Evan (DeltaTech): we started seeing this at 20:04 UTC, roughly 30% of generation calls failing and others hanging for ~8-15s. failing request id: `req_zeta`. traffic degraded. any interim workaround?

Roxanne (SRE): looking at infra metrics now  there's a big spike in connection timeouts to `cache-prefix-read` cluster at 20:02 UTC. p99 command latency > 7s and a lot of `connection reset` traces. gateway 5xx rate jumped from 0.2% to 7.5% within 3 minutes.

Roxanne (SRE): metric snapshot: 
- cache_conn_resets{cluster="cache-prefix-read"}=1840
- cache_cmd_p99_ms=7300
- gateway_5xx_rate{route="/v1/generate"}=7.5%

Arjun (Eng - Runtime): this looks like the prefix/KV cache reads are blocking request threads when cache nodes misbehave. we have a runtime hotflag `runtime.cache.prefix_reads_enabled` that can be flipped to false to force cache-miss flow. recommend flipping in impacted regions immediately. also we should ensure cache reads are non-blocking and have a short socket timeout so they never stall the request thread.

oncall-bot: incident created: INC-2026-0315-004  "Prefix cache dependency causing generation 5xx/timeouts". severity: high. paging oncall.

Ben (Infra): i see a config rollout at 19:58 UTC that changed memcached client keepalive and connection pooling; initial canary looked fine but the full rollout appears to trigger connection churn on kernels with older TCP tuning. i'm rolling back the client config now.

Marta (Support): can we provide customers a short repro or quick indicator they can check? i'll send to affected accounts.

Arjun (Eng - Runtime): repro curl for customers: 
```
curl -s -D - -o /dev/null -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \n  -d '{"model":"rwd/large","input":"ping"}'
```
If you see `HTTP/1.1 502` or response times >5s and gateway logs show `upstream=memcached` or `cache-prefix-read`, it's the same.

Arjun (Eng - Runtime): mitigation plan: 
1) runtime hotflip: `runtime.cache.prefix_reads_enabled=false` (bypass read path)  immediate mitigation
2) infra rollback of memcached client config (Ben)
3) if necessary, scale model backend to handle higher direct load
4) follow-up: implement non-blocking cache calls + circuit breaker so cache failures don't block request threads; add canary for client config rollouts

Ben (Infra): rollback started at 20:12 UTC. evicting problematic nodes from the ring and rejoining last-known-good. restarting affected cache daemons if healthchecks don't pass within 5m.

Roxanne (SRE): applying runtime bypass in eu-central-1 and us-west-2 now. will monitor gateway 5xx and cache error metrics.

Roxanne (SRE): update 20:16 UTC  bypass applied in target regions. gateway 5xx rate dropping; p95 latency improving. cache connection reset rate falling as we isolate affected nodes.

Felix (Support Lead): Marta, please prepare a short status message for status.redwood.ai summarizing impact, mitigation, and request that customers share `X-Request-ID` for outstanding errors. non-technical wording.

Marta (Support): draft: "We are experiencing elevated errors and timeouts for text generation requests in some regions. Our team has applied a temporary mitigation to route around a caching dependency and traffic is recovering. If you continue to see errors, please share the X-Request-ID and region. We will post further updates shortly."

Ben (Infra): rollback completed at 20:21 UTC. cache cluster rebalanced; unhealthy nodes drained. connection resets falling to baseline.

Roxanne (SRE): 20:25 UTC  gateways back to normal error rates in targeted regions. leaving runtime bypass enabled for 10 more minutes to ensure stability before flipping back.

Evan (DeltaTech): confirmed recovery on our side, thanks. appreciate the fast response.

Arjun (Eng - Runtime): follow-ups / action items: 
- implement non-blocking cache read + circuit-breaker (high priority)
- add canary and traffic-sim healthcheck for client config rollouts (no wide rollouts without canary)
- enrich telemetry to correlate cache errors with `X-Request-ID` automatically so support can triage faster

Marta (Support): closing loop with customers, will share postmortem when available. thanks team :thumbsup:

Roxanne (SRE): final note 20:30 UTC  incident marked resolved, monitoring. postmortem will be published tomorrow with timeline and planned mitigations.
